'''Peter Anthony Butler''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FInstP}} (born 22 November 1949) is a [[Professor]] of [[Physics]] at the [[University of Liverpool]].<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2019 for "substantial contributions to the improvement of natural knowledge".<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424061342/https://royalsociety.org/people/peter-butler-14082/ |archivedate=2019-04-24|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/peter-butler-14082/ |publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|title=Professor Peter Butler FRS|author=Anon|year=2015}}</ref>

He was educated at [[Borden Grammar School]], [[King's College London]] (BSc) and the [[University of Liverpool]] (PhD, 1974).<ref>"Butler, Prof. Peter Anthony, (born 22 Nov. 1949), Professor of Physics, since 1999 and Senior Research Fellow, since 2015, University of Liverpool." WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO. 1 Dec. 2019; Accessed 7 Dec. 2019.</ref>

His research area is experimental nuclear physics, especially structure of heavy nuclei. He led a group at [[ISOLDE]] at [[CERN]] who confirmed static octupole form (pear shape) of <sup>224</sup>Ra nuclei.<ref>L. P. Gaffney, P. A. Butler u.a., Studies of pear-shaped nuclei using accelerated radioactive beams, Nature, Band 497, 2013, S. 199-204, [https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12073 Abstract]</ref><ref>[https://physicsworld.com/a/nuclear-physics-goes-pear-shaped/ Hamish Johnston, Nuclear physics goes pear-shaped], Physics World, 8. Mai 2013</ref>
